75.0% GM held in Q2; Q3 guided 74.0%; ~$99B buyback authorisation remaining; ~$26B returned in Q2.

Downgraded 0 -> -1 on evidence, not inference. Q2 OCF $24,077M vs NI $59,688M (40%); H1 63%; Q1 alone 86%. AR $40.7B -> $63.1B in one quarter; AR/quarterly revenue 0.66 (0.50 at Q1). Inventory $31,575M with $784M provisions in Q2. The gap is working capital, not margin, but the working capital is credit extended to customers.

New trap leg K7: NVDA is a vendor-financier of its customers (receivables on 90d-1y terms, $42.8B marketable + $47.9B non-marketable equity book incl. CoreWeave ~10% stake and Nebius, $3.3B equity-method infrastructure financiers, SB Energy/OpenAI-affiliated guarantees capped $105B) while the neocloud credit stack reprices (CoreWeave bonds ~79c). Q3 will mark the equity book down. $279B supply commitments make a demand air-pocket land on inventory first.

Price inside the $148.30-222.44 band, 3.7% below the top. Base 5y IRR +8.8% at 214.13 clears the 8% hurdle on the accounting-OE basis for the first time; cash-haircut basis +0.4%. Forward P/E ~17.9x. Scored 0 not +1 because the cash basis is still at hurdle-zero.

runner_dissent: The dissent says the obvious thing: the five receivables customers are almost certainly hyperscalers and Oracle, not neoclouds; 90-day-to-one-year terms on ~$100B of quarterly shipments are a commercial choice by a company with ~$57B of cash and securities, not distress; the stock is at ~17.9x forward with 75% gross margins; base IRR clears the hurdle at this price; and the 09-05 card's own words were 'the first STARTER candidate this book has had in this complex'. The discipline answer: that card put the cash-flow statement ahead of the entry on purpose; the statement came and did not close the gap; the names on the receivables ledger are not disclosed; and four weeks to the Q3 print is a bounded cost. Better four weeks late than sized on a cash conversion the filing does not yet show.
